html:
An English company chartered in 1670 by King Charles II to trade for furs around Hudson Bay. It lasted more than 350 years, one of the oldest companies in the world.

The charter gave it a vast territory called Rupert's Land, all the land whose rivers drain into Hudson Bay. That was more than a third of modern Canada. The idea came from two French traders from New France, Radisson and Groseilliers.

For two centuries its posts on the bay traded with the Cree and other First Nations, who brought beaver pelts for European hats in exchange for guns, kettles, knives and wool blankets. It competed fiercely with French traders and later with the Montreal based North West Company, which it absorbed in 1821. The fur trade drew maps, routes and alliances across the north of the continent.

In 1870 the company sold Rupert's Land to the new country of Canada. It then became a chain of department stores. After years of decline it went bankrupt, and its last stores closed in 2025.
sum: An English company chartered in 1670 by King Charles II to trade for furs around Hudson Bay. It lasted more than 350 years, one of the oldest companies in the world.
